title: Wine Wimsey Review · Sat Nov 28
subtitle: NEW-VOICE batch 6. Replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 28 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder. 8 character feed posts (4 then-vs-now two-panel story cards in slots 1,3,5,7; 3 rip-off posts and 1 manners/common-sense card) + 2 stories (lipstick then-vs-now and ice-bag rip-off, both second redos). Zero plain cards. Stories remade twice Nov 27 after Scott rejected the original streetlight/car-wash pair and then the porch/towel pair. Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and 2 stories and said upload on Nov 27 at 4:40 PM CST. First-comment delays randomized (0-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: In 1985 a bag boy named Tommy carried my groceries to the car. / Now I scan and bag everything myself, and the machine yells 'unexpected item in bagging area.' / It was my purse.
posts.caption: Tommy had a paper hat and called everybody ma'am. Yesterday the self-checkout froze twice, a teenager came over to type in a code, and I still paid full price for doing his job.
posts.first: I put the purse on the floor and it let me finish. Tommy would never have treated my purse like a criminal.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her smiling as Tommy the bag boy loads grocery bags into her station wagon; now: slow eye-roll at the self-checkout, purse on the bagging shelf). posts.quote: The dentist charged me a $50 'missed appointment fee.' / I was sitting in the waiting room. / Brenda forgot to check me in.
posts.caption: I was there for 45 minutes. I read a 2019 magazine cover to cover, learned about a celebrity divorce that was already over, and watched three people go back ahead of me.
posts.first: They took the fee off after I showed them my parking receipt. I'm keeping that receipt forever.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (one raised eyebrow smirk, holding the $50 no-show bill up like evidence in the dentist waiting room). Text at the top reads: The dentist charged me a $50 'missed appointment fee.' i was sitting in the waiting room. A teal box at the bottom reads: Brenda forgot to check me in.

posts.quote: In 1980 my sister Carol and I saw a concert from the sixth row for $12.50. / Now it's $189 plus a $42 'service fee' / and I watched the whole show on the big screen.
posts.caption: In 1980 we got our tickets by standing in line at the record store at 7 AM with a thermos of coffee. This time I sat in an online waiting room for 50 minutes and lost to a robot.
posts.first: Carol still has her ticket stub in a frame. Mine is a QR code that expired.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her and Carol cheering, holding paper ticket stubs; now: tight fake 'everything is fine' smile, holding up her phone in the nosebleed seats). posts.quote: The salesman told me heated seats were included. / They are. For $12 a month after the free trial. / The wires are already in my seat, Todd.
posts.caption: Todd also threw in free floor mats, which turned out to be the ones that already came with the car. He shook my hand like he'd just done me a favor.
posts.first: I wear a sweater and sit on a towel now. It's free and it doesn't need an app.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (open-mouth 'are you kidding me' squint, holding up her phone with the $12/MONTH subscription screen). posts.quote: In 1987 I called the gas company and a woman named Peggy fixed my bill in four minutes. / Now I said 'representative' to a robot nine times. / It hung up on me. Peggy never would have.
posts.caption: Peggy said 'oh honey, that's our mistake' and it was fixed before my coffee got cold. The robot asked me to describe my problem in a few words, then told me it didn't understand all of them.
posts.first: I called back and pressed zero for six minutes straight. A real man named Luis picked up and fixed it in three.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her relaxed on the kitchen wall phone with her checkbook while Peggy fixes the bill; now: twitchy gritted-teeth grimace, phone held out on speaker). posts.quote: If you borrow my truck for one load of mulch, / you bring it back with gas in it. / It was full, Ron. The light is on.
posts.caption: Ron also returned it with the seat pushed all the way back, the radio on a polka station, and half the mulch still in the bed. His yard looks beautiful, I'm told.
posts.first: I filled it up for $71. Ron is getting a Christmas card with the receipt inside.

posts.quote: In 1979 a waitress named Shirley wrote my order on a pad and got it right. / Now I order at a screen, carry my own drink, / and it still asks me for a 25% tip.
posts.caption: Shirley refilled my coffee before I knew I wanted more and called my dad 'hon.' Today I ordered a muffin at a kiosk, waited for my name, and the screen spun around at me before I even had a napkin.
posts.first: I pressed 'No tip' and the girl behind the counter looked at me like I kicked a puppy. I left two dollars in the jar to feel better.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her smiling as Shirley the waitress writes her order on a pad at the diner; now: side-eye over glasses pulled down her nose, pointing at the tip screen while carrying her own drink). posts.quote: My sister Joan and I split one entree because it could feed a horse. / They charged us a $4 'split plate fee.' / For a second fork.
posts.caption: The plate was a $24 chicken dish the size of a hubcap, and we still took half of it home. Nobody cut it for us. Nobody brought a second plate. Just the fork.
posts.first: Joan kept the fork in her purse. She says we paid for it.
